title: Being unramified descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02VM)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] (locally of finite type with diagonal $X\times_SS_i\to(X\times_SS_i)\times_{S_i}(X\times_SS_i)$ an open immersion) for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is unramified.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02VM (lemma-descending-property-unramified, line 6187: 'The property P(f) = "f is unramified" is fpqc local on the base'), first assertion, the direction 'each base change has the property => f has it' of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310); its proof: unramified = locally of finite type with diagonal an open immersion (Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02GE), and locally of finite type and open immersion are fpqc local on the base (Lemmas Tag 02KX, 02L3)

proof.text: *Step 1 ($f$ is locally of finite type; Descent 02KX).* Write $X_i=X\times_SS_i$ with projections $g_i':X_i\to X$ and $f_i:X_i\to S_i$, $f\circ g_i'=g_i\circ f_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By hypothesis every $f_i$ is unramified, so by [def-weil-unramified-morphism] every $f_i$ is locally of finite type and its diagonal $\Delta_{f_i}:X_i\to X_i\times_{S_i}X_i$ is an open immersion. Since every $f_i$ is locally of finite type and $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], $f$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-type] (applied to $f$ and the same covering). (Source: 'unramified iff locally of finite type and its diagonal is an open immersion (Morphisms 02GE) ... being locally of finite type ... is fpqc local on the base (Lemma 02KX)'; 02GE is the definition [def-weil-unramified-morphism] in the DAG.)

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02VM (lemma-descending-property-unramified, descent.tex line 6187), proof, lines 6194-6205: 'A morphism is unramified ... if and only if it is locally of finite type ... and its diagonal morphism is an open immersion (see Morphisms, Lemma [02GE]). We have seen already that being locally of finite type ... and an open immersion is fpqc local on the base (Lemmas [02KY], [02KX], and [02L3]). Hence the result follows formally.'

proof.text: *Step 2 ($\Delta_{f_i}$ is, up to an isomorphism of its target, the base change of $\Delta_f$ along $h_i$).* Let $P=X\times_SX$ with structure morphism $\pi=f\circ\mathrm{pr}_1:P\to S$ and diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to P$, so $\pi\circ\Delta_f=f$. For $i\in I$ let $P_i=P\times_SS_i$ be the fibre product of $\pi$ and $g_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $h_i:P_i\to P$ and $\pi_i:P_i\to S_i$. Since $\pi\circ(\Delta_f\circ g_i')=f\circ g_i'=g_i\circ f_i$, the universal property of $P_i$ gives a unique $\delta_i:X_i\to P_i$ with $h_i\circ\delta_i=\Delta_f\circ g_i'$ and $\pi_i\circ\delta_i=f_i$ (this is $\Delta_f\times_S\mathrm{id}_{S_i}$). (a) By [lemma-nagata-diagonal-base-change] (with $X_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ the morphism $f:X\to S$ and $S\to S_\lambda$ the morphism $g_i:S_i\to S$; its Lean is CategoryTheory.Limits.diagonal_pullback_fst), the base change $\delta_i$ of $\Delta_f$ is canonically identified with $\Delta_{f_i}$: there is an isomorphism of schemes $c_i:X_i\times_{S_i}X_i\to P_i$ (the canonical identification $(X\times_SS_i)\times_{S_i}(X\times_SS_i)\cong(X\times_SX)\times_SS_i$) with $c_i\circ\Delta_{f_i}=\delta_i$. (b) The square with top $g_i':X_i\to X$, left $\delta_i$, right $\Delta_f$ and bottom $h_i$ commutes and is cartesian: it sits on top of the cartesian square $(P_i,h_i,\pi_i)$ of $\pi$ and $g_i$, and the outer rectangle consists of $g_i'$, $\pi_i\circ\delta_i=f_i$, $\pi\circ\Delta_f=f$ and $g_i$, which is cartesian because $(X_i,g_i',f_i)$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $g_i$; so by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the upper square is cartesian, i.e. $(X_i,g_i',\delta_i)$ is a fibre product of $\Delta_f$ and $h_i$. (Source: the diagonal of $f_i$ is the base change of the diagonal of $f$, which 02VM's 'the result follows formally' leaves implicit; the same identification is written in the proof of Descent 02KU: 'Note that $\Delta'$ is the base change of $\Delta$ via $S'\to S$'.)

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02VM (lemma-descending-property-unramified, descent.tex line 6187), proof, lines 6194-6205: 'A morphism is unramified ... if and only if it is locally of finite type ... and its diagonal morphism is an open immersion (see Morphisms, Lemma [02GE]). We have seen already that being locally of finite type ... and an open immersion is fpqc local on the base (Lemmas [02KY], [02KX], and [02L3]). Hence the result follows formally.'; Descent, Lemma Tag 02KU (lemma-descending-property-separated), proof, line 5598: 'Note that $\Delta'$ is the base change of $\Delta:X\to X\times_SX$ via $S'\to S$'

proof.text: *Step 3 ($\delta_i$ is an open immersion).* By step 1, $\Delta_{f_i}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]: a homeomorphism of $X_i$ onto an open subset $W_i\subseteq X_i\times_{S_i}X_i$ with $\Delta_{f_i}^{-1}\mathcal O_{X_i\times_{S_i}X_i}\to\mathcal O_{X_i}$ an isomorphism. The isomorphism of schemes $c_i$ of step 2(a) is a homeomorphism with $c_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{P_i}\to\mathcal O_{X_i\times_{S_i}X_i}$ an isomorphism [def-pc-scheme]. Hence $\delta_i=c_i\circ\Delta_{f_i}$ is a homeomorphism of $X_i$ onto $c_i(W_i)$, which is open in $P_i$ because $c_i$ is a homeomorphism, and $\delta_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{P_i}=\Delta_{f_i}^{-1}c_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{P_i}\to\Delta_{f_i}^{-1}\mathcal O_{X_i\times_{S_i}X_i}\to\mathcal O_{X_i}$ is the composite of $\Delta_{f_i}^{-1}$ applied to an isomorphism and an isomorphism, hence an isomorphism. So $\delta_i$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].

We have seen already that being locally of finite type ... and an open immersion is fpqc local on the base (Lemmas [02KY], [02KX], and [02L3]). Hence the result follows formally.'

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\{h_i:P_i\to P\}_{i\in I}$ is an fpqc covering of $P$).* Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] with $U=P$, the morphism $\pi:P\to S$ and the fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: the first projections $h_i:P\times_SS_i=P_i\to P$ form an fpqc covering of $P$. (Source: the family $\{X_i\times_{S_i}X_i\to X\times_SX\}$ to which 02VM's 'follows formally' applies 02L3; through the isomorphisms $c_i$ it is the family $\{h_i\}$.)

source.place: Topologies, Lemma Tag 022D (lemma-fpqc), part (3), lines 3105-3147 (base change of an fpqc covering), used implicitly in the proof of Descent 02VM (descent.tex lines 6194-6205) when 02L3 is applied to the diagonal

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\Delta_f$ is an open immersion; Descent 02L3).* Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-open-immersion] to $\varphi=\Delta_f:X\to P$, the fpqc covering $\{h_i:P_i\to P\}_{i\in I}$ of step 4 and, for every $i$, the fibre product $(X_i,g_i',\delta_i)$ of $\Delta_f$ and $h_i$ of step 2(b). Its hypothesis, that every $\delta_i$ is an open immersion, is step 3. Hence $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_SX$ is an open immersion. (Source: 'being ... an open immersion is fpqc local on the base (Lemma 02L3)'.)

We have seen already that being locally of finite type ... and an open immersion is fpqc local on the base (Lemmas [02KY], [02KX], and [02L3]). Hence the result follows formally.'

proof.text: *Step 6 (conclusion).* By step 1 $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and by step 5 its diagonal $\Delta_f$ is an open immersion; so $f$ is unramified by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. (Source: 'Hence the result follows formally.')
